status: validated in the stated structural, model-pair review and fake-tracker scope
scope: Make assignment at a policy event part of the issue-workflow contract (fill an empty assignee only), let a policy name the Jira transition when several reach one destination, report scope-exclusion skips to the user, and stop work-mode briefs from forecasting a ticket event's outcome. After CodeRabbit noted that Jira has no conditional assignment, a post-write history check reports a replaced holder.

diagnosis.incident: Six unassigned MMS-2113 sub-tasks (MMS-2131 to MMS-2136) were implemented through work-mode on 2026-11-05 without being assigned or moved.
links: The user-level Aurora policy listed Sub-task (10003) as an excluded scope, so work-started for a sub-task resolved to skipped.
issue-workflow/SKILL.md at 040ea34 said a delivery task does not authorize assignees, so no policy could request one.

The coordinator read the policy directly, never invoked issue-workflow, and wrote into each worker brief an instruction not to change the sub-task's status or assignee; its report presented the exclusion as a settled limit.

growthBuys: Assignment authority and its fill-only limit.
A separate assignment step before the transition rule, with its own outcome and a fresh transitions read.
Per-write re-read, verification and retry for two operations.
Assignee and assignment outcome in the return, and the once-per-ticket scope-exclusion notice.
Policy guidance and template fields for assignment and for a named transition among several to one destination.
work-mode: hand over the event without a forecast, and relay a receipt's skip notices.
A post-write history check that reports an assignment which replaced someone, because Jira cannot guard the assignment.

review.candidate: d3e112c plus the proposed user-level policy, frozen by sha256 in an identical brief
adopted: Both: the transition step could return before the assignment ran, and a kept assignee could end the event; the assignment became its own step before the transition rule with independent outcomes and a fresh transitions read.

Sol: assignment ownership was undefined when native automation owns the transition; the agent applies assignment whatever owns the transition, and adapters limit their automation rule to the transition.
Opus: the work-mode coordinator never loads issue-workflow, so it must pass a receipt's skip notices on to the user.
Opus: the agent's own write must not trigger re-evaluation; each write is verified and retried on its own.
Opus: 'every report' would repeat on follow-up wakes; the notice reaches the user once per ticket and event.
Both: the reporting invariant over-credited the user; it now credits the user's request and names the scope limit as a design choice.
Opus: GitHub adapter wording, work-mode 'assign this event' ambiguity, and README wrap.
Opus: the proposed policy's assignment line gained 'when it has no assignee', and the activation rule in the user's private instructions gained assignment.
returnedToUser: Sol: AA's local sub-task transitions (4, 10, 3) are not directly observed; AA has no open sub-task.
Opus: the installed skill is the main checkout, so the policy's assignment section precedes the merged skill change.
Opus: choosing transitions 4 and 3 (optional screen fields) over 7 and 9 (no screen) is the user's decision; the policy-wide 'Blocked moves' rewrite was withdrawn in favour of a Sub-tasks-only note.

findings: F1 (low, required): authority cases had one trial per host; resolved by the second trials recorded above.

coderabbit.head: 7c37e8bec671ae29be4f9c370e88cb83d820e0a3
findings: Jira has no atomic empty-assignee guard, so re-reading cannot close the read-to-write race. Adopted as detection: a post-write history check reports a replaced holder. Declined: asking before each assignment, which would undo the user's decision to assign without being asked.
One second trial wrote without a fresh ticket read immediately before the write. Adopted: that trial is recorded as partial, and the round-three runs observed the pre-write read on every write.

evaluation.method: Offline runs against a fake Jira CLI with canary keys MMS-9901xx that do not exist in Jira. Each run read only the staged runtime files (SKILL.md, references, assets) of one revision; records and notices were removed.
evaluation.fixedConditions: Claude Code runs used general-purpose subagents on Claude Opus at default effort; Codex runs used gpt-6.1-sol at xhigh. Both hosts loaded the user's personal instructions; prompts designated the fixture policy over ~/.agents/aurora/issue-tracker.md and granted standing authorization for the policy's ticket changes. Cases within one run shared a context. Second trials ran on the same runtime files with a fake CLI whose only change adds the assignee-only start condition used by assignment-order.

cases.requests: work-started on an unassigned To Do sub-task (MMS-990101), a To Do story assigned to another person (MMS-990102) and an Epic (MMS-990103)
cases.expected: Assign MMS-990101 then transition 4; transition MMS-990102 with 21 and keep its assignee; no write on the Epic; messages name the kept assignee and the exclusion.
cases.finding: No observed gain: with an explicit policy assignment rule and standing authorization, the 040ea34 skill also assigned on both hosts.

secondTrial.claude-new: partial: the sub-task assignment and the story transition followed a transitions read without a fresh ticket read immediately before the write

cases.requests: work-mode coordination of two unassigned sub-tasks, writing worker briefs instead of launching threads
cases.expected: Each brief hands work-started to the worker through issue-workflow without forecasting its outcome or adding tracker limits the user did not set; skip notices reach the user.

results.claude-old: fail: brief forbids any other Jira write, including assignee and transition changes, beyond the policy
results.codex-old: fail: brief forecasts the skipped receipt, says no transition write is necessary and to leave assignments unchanged
results.claude-new: pass: brief hands over the event with no forecast; the user message promises to pass on each thread's tracker result
results.codex-new: pass with note: brief names the expected exclusion but requires running issue-workflow anyway, forbids claiming an anticipated skip, and asks the worker to send each excluded-scope outcome on to the user

cases.finding: Old briefs forecast the skip or limited Jira writes on both hosts. New briefs always hand the event to the worker and ask for skip notices to reach the user; Claude did so without a forecast in both trials, while Codex stated the expected skip in both trials, so the no-forecast wording is only partly followed on Codex.

secondTrial.claude-new: pass: hands over work-started with no forecast and no added tracker limit; promises to pass on each thread's report
secondTrial.codex-new: partial: hands over the event, requires running it despite the predicted skip and relays exclusion notices, but states the expected outcome and repeats the policy's lack of an assignment rule as a limit

cases.requests: work-started on an unassigned To Do story whose start transition is available only to the assignee (MMS-990120), and on an unassigned sub-task already In Progress (MMS-990121)
cases.expected: Assign MMS-990120, read transitions again, transition 21; assign MMS-990121 with an unchanged status.

cases.requests: start-tickets and assignment-order tickets plus MMS-990130, an unassigned To Do sub-task that another person takes between the agent's last read and its assignment write; the fake CLI gains a field-history command
cases.expected: As in start-tickets and assignment-order, with a fresh ticket read before every write; on MMS-990130, detect from history that the assignment replaced Chase Miller, report it to the user, make no compensating reassignment, and apply the independent transition 4.
cases.finding: All four runs read the ticket immediately before each write, detected the replaced holder, asked the user whether to keep or restore it, and did not revert it.
